parsed.modern: 26. A process of wakening is likewise accessory. An action is said to sleep, when it lies over, not limited in for a year, in which case its effect is suspended; but even that it may, at any time within the years of prescription, be served or wakened by a summons, in which the pursuer recites the last step of the process, and concludes that it may be again carried on as if it had not been discontinued. An action that funds upon any of the innerhouse rolls cannot sleep; nor an action in which decree is pronounced, because it has got its full completion: Consequently the decree may be extracted after the year, without the necessity of a wakening
